reason: The cited evidence supports the general accuracy of MLIPs and the efficiency of active learning for training set generation, but it does not provide specific prior results on capturing anharmonicity, electron–vibration coupling, or free-energy landscapes near melting, nor does it demonstrate the claimed speed-up for fusion property calculations.
premises: MLIPs trained on ab initio data can reach near-DFT accuracy for elemental and multicomponent systems
Active learning can automatically generate training sets tailored to specific systems and properties, covering relevant configurational space with minimal DFT calculations
Active learning can target rare anharmonic events and electron–vibration coupling effects near the fusion point
The MLIP surrogate can reproduce the full free-energy landscape including vibrational entropy contributions across the fusion transition
The approach will reduce computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD
